full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim J: This rule was issued on 28-2-2001 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the proceedings of CR Case No. 188 of 2011 under sections 467/471 of the Penal Code, now pending in the Court of Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, 4th Court, Dhaka should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The relevant facts for the purpose of the disposal of the rule are that the opposite party No. 2 as complainant filed a complaint petition being CR Case No. 188 of 2011 on 21-3-2011 in the court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka against the accused-petitioner under sections 467/471/420/109 of the Penal Code stating the fact that the schedule property being Plot No. 34, Block-D, Road No. 100 of Gulshan Model Town measuring an area of 16 kathas was allotted by the Rajuk infavour of Belal Miah, father of the complainant and the accused. Accordingly, Deed of Lease was executed between Rajuk and the lessee, Belal Miah on 2-11-1965. Thereafter, Belal Miah, gifted the schedule plot to his wife Mosammat Majeda Khatun vide registered Heba Deed dated 26-6-1983. Who after mutating her name in Rajuk, gifted the said plot to her two sons, the complainant and the accused by two registered Heba Deed dated 6-7-1985 in equal share, where each son got 8 kathas which was mutated accordingly, but no partition was effected. Thereafter, the complainant submitted an application on 22-1-2008 to Rajuk for partition but the accused did not appear before the Rajuk. Thereafter, the accused submitted a map to Rajuk containing forged signature of the complainant for illegal benefit against which the complainant has serious objection. He further alleged that the complainant is deprived of the main thoroughfare. So partition should be made where both the co-sharer will get the benefit of the main thorough fare. Since the accused is proceeding with the construction work without partitioning the property, who obtained the sanctioned plan from Rajuk by forging the signature in the hand map submitted in Rajuk at the time of splitting the plot, the complainant has serious objection in respect of splitting the plot. The said plot must be partitioned in two equal shares from the main road. In such circumstances the complainant is constrained to file the present petition of complaint. The accused filed a hand map at the time of filing of mutation application before Rajuk for splitting the original Plot No. 34 as per Heba deed, by forgoing the signature of the complainant. 

 6. It may be noted that pursuant to the Rule, complainant-opposite party No. 2 appeared in the present case through his Learned Advocate Mr Monir Hossain by filing Vokalatnama on 7-12-2016, thereafter the case was ready for hearing. On 14-12-2016 learned Advocate for the petitioner, Mr Saifur Reza fixed this matter for hearing. On 8-2-2017 matter was heard in part and Mr Monir Hossain, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the opposite party No. 2. On 12-3-2017, Mr Asif Imtiaz Khan, the learned Advocate filed fresh power in court for the opposite party No. 2 with no objection certificate. Subsequently, on 21-5-2017 Mr Md Jahangir Zammader, the learned Advocate filed a power in court on behalf of the petitioner with no objection certificate issued by the petitioner's filing Advocate Mr Saifur Reza. Ultimately, matter was heard on 3-4-2018 at length and the learned Advocate for the petitioner appeared before this court but no one appears for the opposite party No. 2. After conclusion of the hearing matter was fixed for pronouncement of judgment on 9-5-2018, but no one appears for the opposite party No. 2 on that day. 

 7. The opposite party No. 2 contested the present case by filing Affidavit-in-opposition dated 8-12-2016 denying the material allegations made in the application and contending, inter-alia, that the opposite party No. 2 late Bellal Mia @ Bellal Sarder was allotted plot No. 34 measuring area of 15 (Fifteen) Katha 4 (Four) Chattak, the land in question under an indenture of lease on 2-11-1965 and the said property was gifted to his wife, Mosammat Majeda Khatun by way of registered Heba Deed being No. 9919 dated 26-6-1983. Thereafter, Mosammat Majeda Khatun mutated the said property in her name and she then gifted 8 (Eight) Katha out of 15 (Fifteen) Katha 4 (Four) Chattak to the opposite party No. 2 from the eastern side of the property including one storied building over the land by way of registered Heba Deed being No. 14762 on 3-7-1985 and rest of the property gifted to accused-petitioner by the same way. It is here to mention that the opposite party No. 2 mutated the property in his name in accordance with the Heba Deed and owning and possessing the land in question peacefully since then. In the mean time the accused petitioner applied to the Rajuk for per-mission of a plan to build multi-storied building forging the signature of the opposite party No. 2 and the opposite party No. 2 made representation to the Rajuk complaining against the accused petitioner. Thereafter, the Rajuk investigated the matter and found the documents and deed were being forged by the accused petitioner and thereby the opposite party No. 2 instituted CR Case No. 188 of 2011 before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Adalat and the learned court below framed charge against the accused-petitioners. 

 8. It is further stated that the accused petitioner applied to the Rajuk for plan permission to build a multi-storied using false signature of the opposite party No. 2 which was proved by an investigation carried by the Rajuk and on the basis of the said forgery, the opposite party No. 2 instituted suit and the learned court below took the cognizance. That the CR Case No. 188 of 2011 and Title Suit No. 202 of 2011 is entirely different in nature, so there is no bar in law to take cognizance in the CR case. 

 9. It is also stated that the accused petitioner cannot get 8 Katha of land from the land in question as total area of the said land is 15 Katha and 4 Chattak, even if the land is being divided equally. However, the opposite party No. 2 obtained possession of 8 Katha land along with 10 feet with road out of 30 feet road up to the house of the opposite party No. 2. 

 10. The opposite party No. 2 further filed Supplementary-Affidavit-in-opposition dated 23-1-2017 stating the facts that the opposite party No. 2 filed Title Suit No. 35 of 2016 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka impleading the accused petitioner, Rajuk and others as defendants for permanent injunction against the defendants Nos. 1 and 2 from making illegal and risky construction in violation of the law of construction. 

 11. Mr Omar Sadat, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused petitioner after placing the petition of complaint submits that the allegations made in the petition of complaint, even if, are taken as true do not constitute an offence punishable under sections 467/471 of the Penal Code. He further submits that the complainant in paragraph No. 5 of the complaint petition categorically stated that: “তফসিল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তিতে সঠিক ও ছাহাম না করিয়া বেআইনীভাবে জাল স্বাক্ষর করিয়া সৃজনকৃত নক্সায় জাল স্বাক্ষরিত নক্সাটি রাজধানী সর্তৃপক্ষকে প্রভাবিত করিয়া আদেশ করিয়াছে যাহা অন্যায়ভাবে করিয়াছে”। Thus it is apparent that the complainant claimed that the accused-petitioner by forging the signature of the opposite party No. 2 obtained a map by influencing the Rajuk authority, without partitioning the schedule property. 

 12. He next submits that the opposite party No. 2 filed this complaint petition on total misconception stating that the Rajuk approved the Deed of Gift and split the plot No. 34 into two saham, being plot Nos. 34A and 34B. But in fact Rajuk in terms of the aforesaid two Heba Deeds and on the prayer of both the parties mutated their names as lessees of Rajuk by Memo dated 29-12-1998, which contained a map prepared and drawn by the Rajuk and same was accepted by both the parties by putting their respective signature in the said map long before 13 years. The learned Advocate for the petitioner by referring section 464 of the Penal Code submits that no ingredients of the offence of making false documents and forgery as defined in the sections 464/463 have been disclosed in the complaint petition against the accused petitioner in respect of the offence punishable under sections 467/468/471 of the Penal Code. Section 471 speaks about the offence when this forged document is used as genuine document which he knows or has reason to believe to be a forged document. 

 13. We have heard the learned Advocate for the petitioner, perused the application, Supplementary Affidavits dated 10-3-2017, 20-5-2017, 28-5-2017, 10-7-2017, 15-5-2018 and 20-5-2018 filed by the petitioner and Affidavit-in-opposition dated 8-12-2016 and Supplementary Affidavit-in-opposition dated 23-1-2017 filed by opposite party No. 2 and Annexures annexed with the application and documents filed by both the parties. 

 14. It appears that in the present case, the complainant claimed that the accused-petitioner by forging the signature of the complainant filed mutation application to Rajuk by putting his signature in the map and obtained the order of mutation by influencing the Rajuk authority. In fact the map was prepared and drawn by the Rajuk and upon acceptance by the parties, Rajuk just attorned them as lessees as per Heba Deed and splitting the plot No. 34 which was originally allotted to their father and subsequently gifted the same to their mother Mosammat Majeda Khatun, who made two Registered Heba Deed being nos. 14762 dated 6-7-1985 and Heba Deed No. 14763 dated 3-7-1985. By that said two Heba Deeds the opposite party No. 2 was assigned the Eastern side together with one storied building over the land and the accused-petitioner was assigned the Western side of the said plot No. 34. The Lessor-Rajuk as per Heba Deed executed by their mother-Lessee, simply attorned the complainant and the accused as its Lessees and split the plot No. 34 into two plots being No. 34A in the saham of the accused-petitioner measuring an area of 7 katha, 6 chattak 42 square feet and plot No. 34B in the saham of opposite party No. 2, Md Soaib, measuring an area of 6 katha, 8 chattak and 34 square feet which was shown in the map prepared by Lessor-Rajuk and the partition was accepted by them long back on 29-12-1998. Apart from the above, a land of 1 katha, 4 Chataks and 14 Sq. feet was demarcated separately for the internal road between the accused-petitioner and opposite party No. 2’s properties (Annexure-3 series) to the Supplementary Affidavit dated 19-3-2017 filed by the accused-petitioner. So, the question forgery, the element of fraud or dishonesty as alleged against the petitioner in the complaint petition does not lie at all. The act of the accused-petitioner, as has been alleged in the petition of complaint, at best could raise a cause of action for initiating civil action against the accused-petitioner, if by creating the alleged map by forging the signature of the complainant. 

 15. It further appears that both the parties have taken possession of their respective plot of land they obtained by way of gift from their mother. Since the plots was splited by the Rajuk on 29-12-1998 and both the parties accepted the same and enjoying their properties since long. So, we find that no offence has been 'disclosed in the petition of complaint since the map was prepared by Rajuk at the time of splitting their plots is not a valuable security and the accused is not the author of forgery. Thus section 467 of the Penal Code is not attracted to the present case and same is liable to be discharged. 

 16. It is pertinent to note that admittedly the complainant before filing the present complaint petition instituted Title Suit No. 202 of 2011 on 8-3-2011 in the 1st Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka impleading the present accused-petitioner as defendant No. 1 for partition and also for a declaration that the defendant by forging the signature of the plaintiff-complainant in the Rajuk map/plan illegally proceeding construction of the building in the said plot but in the said suit he did not implead the Rajuk as defendant. Although admittedly the schedule plot of land is belonged to Rajuk and mother of the complainant and accused-petitioner being Lessee of the plot No. 34, executed two Heba Deeds dated 3-7-1985 and 6-7-1985 in their favour, accordingly Rajuk accepted the same and they become lessees under the Rajuk on 29-12-1998. It also appears that the allegations made in the petition of complaint (Annexure- A) and the averments made in the plaint of Title Suit No. 202 of 2011 (Annexure- C) are same and the said suit was filed earlier then the petition of complainant, when the civil court are seisin of the matter, criminal court should keep its hands off from such matter and no criminal proceeding should be continued. 

 17. It further appears from Annexure 'D' to the Supplementary Affidavit-in-opposition dated 23-1-2017 filed by the opposite party No. 2 stating the facts that opposite party No. 2 instituted Title Suit No. 35 of 2016 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka impleading the present-accused-petitioner as defendant No. 1, Rajuk and others as defendant Nos. 2-4 for permanent injunction for the self-same plot of land. 

 18. Moreover, from Annexure-6 series of the Supplementary Affidavit dated 19-3-2017 filed by the petitioner, it transpires that the Authorized Officer-2, Rajuk issued Memos dated 15-1-2009, 21-1-2009 and 29-1-2009 upon the opposite party no. 2, Md Soaib, Lessee of the plot No. 34B, Road No. 100, Gulshan directing him to demolish all unauthorized construction of the 3rd floor of the building situated on the said plot No. 34B, without obtaining approved plan from the Rajuk, which clearly proved that the opposite party No. 2 accepted the partition and splitting the plot No. 34 as per Heba Deed executed by his mother Mosammat Majeda Khatun on 29-12-1998. The partition of the said plot was acted upon long 13 years back by all concerned including the lessee of plot No. 34B, the opposite party No. 2. 

 20. As it appears that the complainant opposite-party No. 2 being a private party, lodged the complaint before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka against the accused petitioner under sections 467/471 of the Penal Code alleging that the accused with the connivance of the Rajuk officials forgoing the signature of the complainant prepared a map partitioning the plot No. 34 which was originally allotted to their father and subsequently gifted the same to their mother, who executed two registered Heba deeds dated 3-7-1985 and 6-7-1985. Accordingly, Rajuk as per Heba Deeds split the said plot into plots being plot No. 34A and 34B and attorned them as lessees of the Rajuk long back on 29-12-1998. The complainant filed a partition suit being Title Suit No. 202 of 2011 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka on 8-3-2011 and since the petition of complaint contains allegations of filing and used of forged documents in the proceedings of a suit, we find that the initiation of a criminal proceedings for forgery at the instant of the complainant-opposite party No. 2 without taking recourse of the procedure provided in section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure is barred.
